title: Serum v3 + OpenBook v1 (Solana): zombie order-book vaults and ~673K SOL of permanently locked dead-market rent — no permissionless extraction path
closed_reasons: settle_funds requires OpenOrders owner signature (openbook/serum state.rs load_orders_mut owner check)
close_open_orders is owner-only and requires zero balances; zeroed OpenOrders shells count = 0
sweep_fees/disable_market require hardcoded authority keys (SigningFeeSweeper / SigningDisableAuthority)
prune requires prune_authority which is None for all V1 markets (0 V2 markets exist)
no CloseMarket instruction in either program: market/bids/asks/event-queue/request-queue/vault rent is permanently locked
program upgrades gated: Serum v3 by FTX-era EOA, OpenBook v1 by dormant SPL-Governance DAO council (8/13 tokens, community mint supply 0)
no Jan-2023 OpenBook vulnerability exists; v1 frozen 2022-12, never audited, no advisories; OtterSec critical was v2 (fixed)

poc.note: Solana target: gates proven by deployed-source audit + live account state (RPC); CI job re-verifies state into ci-out/state_check.json (exit=0). No tx simulation executed. Deployed ELF embeds source_revision 546e5fe = v0.5.10, so audited source == deployed bytecode.

caveats: OpenBook v1 is unaudited frozen code; residual unknown-bug risk is why confidence is medium not high
Serum v3 registry covers 168 markets; DefiLlama full set is larger (state TVL $17.13M), so H-O/P figures are conservative lower bounds

No tx simulation executed; gates proven from deployed source + live account state; deployed ELF = v0.5.10 (source_revision 546e5fe)
OpenOrders count 802,133 is exact, but not all were individually checked for emptiness/owner liveness; the ~18,736 SOL closable-rent figure assumes all are empty and owner-controlled
one_liner: external unprivileged attacker can extract ~$0 live from Serum v3/OpenBook v1: vault payouts need the OpenOrders owner's signature, fee sweeps/upgrades are key- or DAO-gated, zeroed OpenOrders shells (the one claimable rent path) count 0, and ~673K SOL ($81M) of dead-market rent is permanently locked with no close instruction.
